subject: Agricultural Science
sourceFile: Copy of Prevocational Studies BECE Syllabus - syllabusNG.txt
examFormat: Pre-Vocational Studies (PVS) integrates Agriculture and Home Economics; it aims to develop candidates' interest in Agriculture and Home Economics, help them acquire basic knowledge, enlighten them on the occupational areas in Pre-Vocational Studies, and appreciate the dignity of labour and entrepreneurship. BECE Pre-Vocational Studies has two compulsory papers of sixty multiple-choice questions each, lasting one hour each; together they are weighted 70%, with 30% from school Continuous Assessment. Agriculture is examined in Paper 1: sixty multiple-choice questions in one hour.
excluded: Left out the syllabus.ng "About Us", "About BECE", eligibility, grading, registration, table of contents and FAQ chapters (publisher marketing / general information, not syllabus content). The Home Economics theme (Paper 2) is in its own file.
recommendedTexts: Seagrove Pre-Vocational Studies for Schools and Colleges, Books 1, 2 and 3 — Emmanuel O. Onazi and Afolabi I. Ademola (Seagrove Publishers Limited, Ibadan)
Essentials of Agricultural Science for Junior Secondary Schools in West Africa — Earnest Chukwudi Anie (Anie with G.O. Enterprises, Ikeja, Lagos)
Intensive Agricultural Science for Junior Secondary Schools — E. U. Okam (Elite Publishers, Onitsha)

topics.name: Importance and Forms of Agriculture
objectives: Explain the importance of agriculture in the society, e.g. source of food, clothing etc.
Identify types of agricultural practices in the localities, e.g. pastoral farming, arable farming etc.
Identify forms of agricultural activities in the communities: growing of crops, rearing of livestock, rearing of fish, apiculture (bee farming) and snail rearing (snailery)
topics.content: Sub-theme: Concept and Medium of Agricultural Production.

topics.name: Classes and Uses of Crops
objectives: Distinguish crop plant forms: monocotyledons (e.g. maize, guinea corn) and dicotyledons (e.g. cowpea, melon)
Classify crops based on life span and uses
Classify crops as sources of carbohydrate, protein, fats and oil, minerals and vitamins
topics.content: Sub-theme: Concept and Medium of Agricultural Production.

topics.name: Classes and Uses of Farm Animals
objectives: Identify types of farm animals: work animals, dairy animals, guard animals, poultry, aquatic animals, pets etc.
Describe the basic characteristics of farm animals
Classify farm animals based on size, habitat, mammals and non-mammals, stomach types and uses
topics.content: Sub-theme: Concept and Medium of Agricultural Production.

topics.name: Methods of Weed and Pest Control
objectives: State the characteristics of weeds, e.g. easily dispersed, long dormancy
State the uses of weeds, e.g. medicinal, food etc.
Describe methods of weed control, e.g. crop rotation, herbicides etc.
Explain the effects of weed control methods on vegetation and soil: pollution of soil and ground water, contamination of livestock pasture etc.
Classify insect pests based on mouth parts: piercing and sucking insects; biting and chewing insects
Describe the damage done by crop pests
Explain the effects of crop pests on yield
topics.content: Sub-theme: Concept and Medium of Agricultural Production.

topics.name: Factors of Agricultural Production
objectives: Identify the factors of agricultural production: land, labour, water, money and management
topics.content: Sub-theme: Concept and Medium of Agricultural Production.

topics.name: Farm Structures and Buildings
objectives: Describe farm structures and farm buildings
State the uses of farm structures and farm buildings
Explain the maintenance of farm structures and farm buildings

topics.name: Crop Propagation and Cultural Practices
objectives: Explain the meaning of propagation
Describe methods of crop propagation: by seed (sexual) and by vegetative organs (asexual)
State the advantages of propagation by seed and by vegetative organs
State the disadvantages of propagation by seed and by vegetative organs

topics.name: Agricultural Practices
objectives: Describe pre-planting operations: choice of site, clearing, stumping, plotting, tilling, seed selection, nursery and nursery practices
Describe planting operations: seed treatment, spacing and planting
Describe post-planting operations: thinning, supplying, mulching, manuring/fertilizer application and harvesting
Explain the effects of timely harvesting versus late harvesting
Describe post-harvest operations: processing of crops into usable forms and storage

topics.name: Animal Feeds and Feeding
objectives: Explain the meaning of feed
Identify types of feed: energy-yielding feeds and protein-yielding feeds
Identify feeding tools: troughs, drinker sets etc.

topics.name: Animal Pests and Disease Control
objectives: Identify farm animal diseases: bacterial, fungal, viral, protozoan, worms (all farm animals) and nutritional such as bloat
Describe modes of transmission of farm animal diseases: contact with infected animals, discharges, vectors (e.g. tsetse fly) etc.
Describe the symptoms of farm animal diseases
Explain the effects of diseases on farm animals: reduced productivity, loss of appetite, loss of weight, death etc.
Describe methods of prevention and control: good sanitation, medication/immunisation, isolation/disposal etc.

topics.name: Fishery
objectives: Define fishery
Classify fish based on habitat (fresh water and salt water fish), morphology (bony and cartilaginous fish) and other types of aquatic organisms
State the uses of fish and fish products
Describe methods of fishing
Explain risk factors in water and fish farming: polluting water with chemicals/industrial effluents; contaminating fish with chemicals used for catching fish

topics.name: Forest and Forest Uses
objectives: Identify types of forest: mangrove (swampy), rain forest (many trees) and derived forest (few trees)
Identify forest resources: trees, wildlife (animals), fruits (foodstuff), herbs and shelter
State the uses of forest resources
Explain the effects of forest on the environment
Describe human activities that affect the forest: clearing/deforestation, hunting, bush burning, farming
Explain depletion of wildlife

topics.name: Packaging Criteria
objectives: State packaging criteria: nature of the produce (liquid or solid, and shape), bulkiness (size), live, frozen or dry stock, and distance to market
Give examples of packaging items: boxes, drums/barrels, cages, polythene, trays etc.

topics.name: Pricing and Advertising
objectives: Define pricing
Identify price determinants: cost of production, quality of produce, quantity of produce, forces of demand and supply, market price and seasonal produce

topics.name: Records and Book Keeping
objectives: Define farm records
Use farm records to monitor the progress of the business
Identify types and uses of farm records: farm diary, farm inventory, input records, production records, consumption records, sales records, profit and loss account
Explain computer-aided farm records and their benefits
Define book keeping
Identify source documents: sales invoice, purchase invoice, returns inwards and returns outwards
Prepare journals, e.g. sales journal, purchase journal

topics.name: Agriculture in Stock Exchange
objectives: Explain the meaning of stock exchange
Identify people involved in the stock exchange: buyers, sellers, buyers and sellers, farmers' agents
State the importance of the stock exchange in agriculture: encourages investment in agriculture and encourages contract farming

topics.name: Export Promotion in Agriculture
objectives: Explain the meaning of export promotion
Give examples of Nigerian export produce: cocoa, palm produce, hides and skins, cassava, groundnut, pepper etc.
State the benefits of export promotion: attracts foreign money (exchange) and serves as an additional market outlet for farmers to earn income
